references.text: Jacob had a meeting with God at Bethel, where he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, and God gave him promises. Later he built an altar there and called the place Bethel.
God commanded Jacob to go to Bethel and build an altar there for God who revealed himself to him when he fled from Esau. Jacob urged his people to purify themselves before the journey.
Abraham built an altar near Bethel and called on the name of the Lord, making Bethel an important holy place already from the time of the patriarchs.
Rebekah advised Jacob to flee to Laban in Haran to escape Esau's anger – the flight that the verse refers to with 'when he fled from his brother'.
Hosea refers to Jacob's meeting with God at Bethel, where God spoke with him – a prophetic look back on the event in Genesis 35:7.
Parallel in the naming of altars that testify to God's revelation to Jacob.
Direct narrative connection where 35:1 is God's command and 35:7 is the fulfillment of the same event.
Theological contrast between Jacob's holy altar to the Lord and Ahab's idolatrous altar for Baal.
Contrast between obedience at Bethel and ungodliness in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
Thematic parallel between Isaac and Jacob, both marking God's presence by building altars.
Theological parallel between Abraham's and Jacob's revelations at Bethel as a basis for building altars.
Connects Jacob's altar at Bethel with Abraham's original altar on the same site.
Direct narrative connection where 35:15 confirms the naming of the place in 35:7.
